label: churn100-s0
summary: The model predicts churn for a telecom customer from three behaviours. Customer service calls: from three calls up, three parts open together, so at the typical customer predicted risk goes from 2% at two calls to 13% at four and 85% at six; one of these parts (low_day_use_service_calls) is stronger for customers with few daytime minutes. Heavy use: day charge combined with evening minutes (heavy_day_eve_use) and day charge without voice-mail messages (day_charge_without_voicemail) raise risk; the 1083 training customers with the heavy-use gate open churn at 26.9% against 9.4%. Plans, through direct linear terms: an international plan raises the typical customer's risk from 2% to 18%, and a voice-mail plan with no messages lowers it to below 1%. A state part adds per-state shifts fitted to state groups of 41 to 81 customers, and two small parts barely change the ranking. Switching off the direct terms drops the training AUC from 0.908 to 0.826, heavy_day_eve_use to 0.878 and low_day_use_service_calls to 0.893.
